applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row, so K-S2's limits on using single-verse silence for UNDERDETERMINED apply.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: 'single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED'—I weighed Reading A (it bars only an UNDERDETERMINED verdict grounded solely on one verse's silence) against Reading B (it bars any UNDERDETERMINED verdict involving a single verse).
why: The judge's underdetermination rests on the competing chains' force, not on Acts 2:30's failure by itself to state the link or its contrary.
